lines.sentence: Another wave of shadows are pushed off, but are just as quickly replaced, finally grasping the bard and bar maid.
Shit, Miss Laurel!
There’s no reason to be so obnoxiously resilient, miss. Just let us guide you-

As the god before them starts to reach out to calm them, a bright light swallows him whole from across the horizon. The shadows surrounding everyone reel back in response as another frame is barely visible within the light.
You haunting shades should know better than to lay your darkness across my city, the City of the Sun. Who was the one that let these creatures within my divine presence?
Who are you?? This is my city.

I see, a mortal has taken it upon themselves to disguise as myself. I hope you know the punishment you ask for merely daring to try this, but for continuing to do so to my face, I will make sure you don’t have to question if what you did was wrong.
Two Ras?
I’ve just returned from battling Apep in the Underworld. I am much too exhausted to humor this right now, I will handle it myself-
Aha! Sounds like an excuse that a mortal would give to impersonate a GOD.

The tired God extended his hand above his head, the sun reaching just above before the light sheds the illusion that the false god let cover them in an instant. The shadows followed suit, evaporating in the light.
Ah… well, I was kind of hoping I could convince the others that I was real.
No. You will not be given that grace. Now then, who gave you this power? It definitely is not the kind that dwells within mortals.
Oho, but you still want information out of me? Well, my journey here was simply to disrupt HER.
…Me?
Indeed! I don’t know what you did, but their royal highness LOVES that you suffer whenever he does anything.
I mean, I barely had to say that I was the god of the sun and look at you! Collapsed on the floor at the hands of some bard you’ve only known for a handful of years!
Have you told him yet? That you’re the God he looks up to so fondly?
Oh Quilla, Goddess of Strings and Stories!
The impersonator quickly started bleeding after his face took impact from a fist.
OW!
Silence fool. Your insults are directed toward Laurel, Pourer of Drinks and Enjoyer of Stories. She has a deep distaste for people of your intention.
I share this distaste.
Then allow him to bother you no longer. I will make sure that I get to see him whenever I go back to the Underworld.
Hey! Don’t touch me!
As for you two, I think your answer lies here.
The God of the Sun grabbed at and took hold of an amulet found around the imposter’s neck. Inscribed on the necklace is the shape of a spider, lodged in its own web and surrounded by norse runes.
A symbol closer. Much better than having to go back to the tavern without anything.
Indeed. Unfortunately the Pact of the Gods prevents me from guiding mortals anymore. I do apologize for what you’ve experienced in my city though, Miss Laurel and Mister Straeon.
Thank you so much, oh God of the Sun…
…Do gods just know our names?
